body:
Welcome, @dylanoliverdo-coder, and thanks for taking #3633. It is a real collision case, and the PR body is well written: the two pinning tests, the replay of the two-boss job, the control job with its moves unchanged, and an honest note on what you could not finish on your host.

What happens next:
1. When you are happy with it, **mark it ready for review** (`gh pr ready 3780`). Reviews start only on ready PRs.
2. It changes how a rapid is checked against the model, so it gets the **safety-tier review**: a full read plus a build and the touched suites on our side, including the app catalog lane that timed out on your machine.
3. If the review asks for changes, push them to the same branch (no force-push) and it is reviewed again. Once it is clean, a maintainer merges it.

If anything in the process is unclear, ask here. AGENTS.md in the repo root has the details.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d330cf02a2f18692fa3338f01ca5f425d8b4ac52 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a safety-tier review: the change sets how the rapid between two Waterline rings is checked against the model.

Thank you, @dylanoliverdo-coder. This is a clean first PR.

### What looks good

- The fix does what #3633 asks. A same-level hop stays at the retract height only when that height is at or above the model top, or when `straight_ok` (the #3627 ball sweep) clears the chord. If not, the hop goes to the clearance height.
- The check uses the real destination of each entry: the ring entry for a plunge, and the ramp start `cs` for a ramp. The column check, the rotation of the ring start, the ramp legs and the moves all use the same `approach_z`. Thus the height that is checked is the height that is cut.
- The safe direction is the default. A non-finite input makes `straight_ok` return `false`, and the hop goes to clearance.
- Level-to-level moves and the first move do not change. They already use clearance or the start position.
- The two pinning tests close the two directions:
  - `waterline_ring_hop_clears_the_boss_and_keeps_a_safe_retract`: retract Z7 under a boss top of Z10 gives a hop at clearance, and `verify_finish` finds no warning. Retract Z13 keeps Z13. The XY chord does not change.
  - `waterline_keeps_a_low_hop_that_clears_the_model`: a distant facet raises the model top above Z13, so the sweep path runs. The sweep clears the chord, and all moves stay the same.
- No unwrap, expect or panic in the new production code. No golden, recorded program or catalog file changed. No UI change, so no screenshots are necessary.
- The commit subject is conventional, the commit body ends `Fixes #3633`, and the PR body has a `Changelog:` line. The decision file `docs/decisions/3633-waterline-ring-clearance.md` records the dropped option ("always use clearance").

### Results, merged with main

Built locally, as a trial merge of `d330cf02a` with upstream/main `db3bb1f7f`. The merge had no conflicts.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 16 steps, 0 failed (1.9 min) |
| Pinning suite `finish3d_hop_height` | 5 passed, both pinning tests included |
| Motion suites `lib`, `finish3d_overhang_and_chord`, `finish3d_waterlines`, `refusal_ghost_frames` | pass |
| App suites `example_catalog` (39 passed, 4 ignored), `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `catalog_groove_part_off`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_4axis_part`, `first_part_programs`, `first_router_part`, `tilt_basis_compat` | pass |
| `catalog_3d_rough_finish::regenerates` and `::rebuilds` (the step that timed out on the author's host) | pass, in debug |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate light` (release) | 6 steps, 0 failed |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` (release, full reach) | 99 steps, 0 failed (19.8 min). This includes `motion heavy: finish3d` (33 passed), `finish3d_gaplink`, and `app heavy: example_catalog` (4 passed). The three known-fail #1950 steps failed as expected. |

Heavy lanes green on d330cf02a2f18692fa3338f01ca5f425d8b4ac52, against upstream/main db3bb1f7f.

**Extra suites run:** none were necessary. The diff does not touch `testdata/` or the import code.

### Mutations (safety tier)

1. `approach_z_at` always returns `nominal_z` (no lift to clearance). Result: RED. `waterline_ring_hop_clears_the_boss_and_keeps_a_safe_retract` fails, and the verifier finds `RapidInStock { at: 19 }` at retract Z7.
2. Skip `straight_ok`, so each same-level hop below the model top goes to clearance. Result: RED. `waterline_keeps_a_low_hop_that_clears_the_model` fails, because the hop moves from Z13 to Z25.

The file is restored after each mutation. The two tests pin the two branches of the new rule.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Notes (not blocking)

1. `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/rings.rs` grows from 542 to 570 lines. It was already larger than the 400-line limit before this PR. A later split can move the entry logic to a module of its own.
2. When the hop goes to clearance, the vertical lift at the end of the previous ring now goes higher. This lift is not checked against the model. That is not a new gap: the level-to-level lift at line 513 also goes to clearance without a check. Under an overhang above the ring end, a higher lift can touch the model. Suggested follow-up: P7.
3. In the rotation search for a closed ring, `approach_z_at` runs `straight_ok` for each candidate vertex, up to about 256 times. This is a small cost because `column_clear` makes the same pass over the supports. No change is necessary.

The PR is already marked ready. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Merging as SAME (no head movement since the counted review). The review that stands: `<!-- pr-reviewer: d330cf02a2f18692fa3338f01ca5f425d8b4ac52 -->` by mkinney, clean at head `d330cf02a2f18692fa3338f01ca5f425d8b4ac52`. Merge commit pinned with `--match-head-commit`.
